meta.title: US Measles Tracker
meta.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the 2026 US measles surge: CDC case counts, cases by state, outbreaks, deaths, elimination status and a dated timeline.
meta.disclaimer: This tracker summarises CDC data, state health departments and news reports. It is not medical advice. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about MMR vaccination, and call ahead before visiting a clinic if you think you have measles.

headline: US measles cases reach 4,588, the most since 1991, CDC says. Pennsylvania's outbreak has reached 1,338 cases and New York has declared a disaster emergency.

status.label: Growing · most since 1991
status.summary: CDC counted 4,588 confirmed cases as of 22 October, 178 more than a week earlier, with 479 hospitalisations and 43 new outbreaks reported in 2026. Pennsylvania's outbreak, centred on Lancaster County, has reached 1,338 cases in 44 counties and five confirmed deaths by the state's count (23 October), while CDC counts three, a figure it confirmed on 20 October. A regional health body will decide in November whether the US has lost the measles elimination status it has held since 2000.

claims.claim: Most 2026 cases are in vaccinated people
claims.detail: 94% of cases were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status as of 4 September, CDC data show. In Pennsylvania, more than 99% of cases were unvaccinated.

claims.claim: The US has already lost its measles elimination status
claims.detail: Not yet. PAHO postponed its review to November 2026 at the US's request. Many experts expect the status to be lost.

claims.claim: Pennsylvania has had five measles deaths this year
claims.detail: Confirmed by the state health department. CDC's national count is three (20 October) because it only counts deaths confirmed through death certificates.

claims.claim: 2026 is the worst US measles year since 1991
claims.detail: 2026 passed 2025's total of 2,289 in July. The 4,588 cases counted by 22 October are the most since 1991's 9,643.

claims.claim: Two doses of MMR vaccine are about 97% effective
claims.detail: CDC: one dose is about 93% effective and two doses about 97%.

timeline.title: PAHO schedules a review of US measles elimination status
timeline.body: The Pan American Health Organization announces a special session to review whether the US and Mexico still meet the bar for measles elimination.

timeline.title: One year since the West Texas outbreak began
timeline.body: The outbreak that began in West Texas on 20 January 2025 marks a year with US cases reported every week. Elimination is lost if one chain of spread lasts 12 months or more.

timeline.title: US passes 1,000 cases for 2026
timeline.body: CDC counts 1,136 confirmed cases as of 26 February, the third time since 2000 that the country has passed 1,000 in a year.

timeline.title: PAHO postpones the elimination review to November
timeline.body: At the US's request, PAHO moves the review to its regular November 2026 meeting while genome sequencing continues.

timeline.title: South Carolina's outbreak declared over
timeline.body: South Carolina ends its Upstate outbreak after 997 cases, 670 of them in 2026, and no deaths.

timeline.title: US passes 2,000 cases for the second year running
timeline.body: CDC counts 2,030 confirmed cases.

timeline.title: 2026 overtakes 2025: the most cases since 1991
timeline.body: CDC counts 2,318 cases as of 23 July, above all of 2025 (2,289) and the highest total since 1991.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania reports its first two measles deaths
timeline.body: Two infants in Lancaster County die of measles-associated illness, the state health department says.

timeline.title: US passes 3,000 cases
timeline.body: CDC counts 3,134 cases, 38 outbreaks and 248 hospitalisations. 94% of cases were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania confirms two more deaths
timeline.body: Deaths in Jefferson and Mifflin counties bring the state's total to four.

timeline.title: CDC confirms two measles deaths nationally
timeline.body: CDC's national count rises to two. It now counts only deaths confirmed through death certificates (NCHS), so it is lower than state tallies.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania reports a fifth death
timeline.body: A fifth measles-associated death is confirmed in Lancaster County.

timeline.title: CDC: 3,887 cases in 47 jurisdictions
timeline.body: The weekly update counts 228 new cases, 42 new outbreaks this year, and 95% of cases linked to outbreaks.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania passes 1,000 cases; New York declares a disaster emergency
timeline.body: Pennsylvania reaches 1,004 cases in 39 counties, the first US state past 1,000 in a year since 1991. New York's governor declares a state disaster emergency through 4 November and lets pharmacists, paramedics and midwives vaccinate.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,078 cases in 41 counties
timeline.body: The state health department's Wednesday update counts 1,078 confirmed cases, 207 hospitalisations and 5 measles-associated deaths. Lancaster County has 401 cases and Mifflin County 153. About 40 of the 74 cases added since 5 October were older infections only recently confirmed, and the department said the update does not reflect a current surge in new infections.

timeline.title: CDC: 4,080 cases in 47 jurisdictions
timeline.body: The weekly update, with data as of 8 October, counts 193 new cases, 42 new outbreaks this year and 414 hospitalisations. CDC counts 2 deaths; Pennsylvania reports 5 under its own definition. The total is the highest for a year since 1991.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,222 cases in 42 counties
timeline.body: The state health department's update counts 1,222 confirmed cases and 5 confirmed measles-associated deaths. The department said it is conducting a review of a death reported by the Franklin County coroner and will update the public when it is complete.

timeline.title: CDC to send more support to Pennsylvania
timeline.body: CDC said it would send additional support to Pennsylvania's outbreak investigation after the state requested help through CDC's Epi-Aid programme.

timeline.title: CDC: 4,410 cases in 47 jurisdictions
timeline.body: The weekly update, with data as of 15 October, counts 4,410 confirmed cases, 42 new outbreaks this year and 451 hospitalisations. 96% of cases are linked to outbreaks. CDC counts 2 deaths; Pennsylvania reports 5 under its own definition. CDC also announced it will send an epidemiologist to support Pennsylvania's investigation.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,260 cases
timeline.body: The state health department's update counts 1,260 confirmed cases, 238 hospitalisations and 5 confirmed measles-associated deaths, with 38 new cases since 14 October. The department has not yet confirmed the death reported by the Franklin County coroner.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,286 cases in 42 counties
timeline.body: The state health department's update counts 1,286 confirmed cases, 247 hospitalisations and 5 confirmed measles-associated deaths, 26 more cases than its previous update on 16 October. The department said it is investigating a further reported death in Franklin County.

timeline.title: CDC confirms a third measles death
timeline.body: CDC added a third measles death to its national count, up from two. Reuters and Al Jazeera report that CDC confirmed it after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate. CDC has not said where the death occurred and says its count could change as reviews continue. Pennsylvania's own count is five.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,317 cases in 43 counties
timeline.body: The state health department's update counts 1,317 confirmed cases in 43 counties, 251 hospitalisations and 5 confirmed measles-associated deaths, 31 more cases than its previous update on 19 October. The department says its nurses have given more than 10,000 MMR vaccine doses to residents across the state in 2026.

timeline.title: CDC: 4,588 cases, 178 more than last week
timeline.body: The weekly update, with data as of 22 October, counts 4,588 confirmed cases, 178 more than a week earlier, with 479 hospitalisations and 43 new outbreaks reported this year. About 96% of cases are linked to outbreaks. CDC counts 3 deaths; Pennsylvania reports 5 under its own definition.

timeline.title: Pennsylvania: 1,338 cases in 44 counties
timeline.body: The state health department's update counts 1,338 confirmed cases in 44 counties, 255 hospitalisations and 5 confirmed measles-associated deaths.

facts.a: Through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. The virus can linger in a room for up to two hours, so people can catch it without direct contact. People are contagious from four days before to four days after the rash appears.
High fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes, followed by a rash that starts on the face. Symptoms usually appear 7 to 14 days after exposure.
About 1 in 5 unvaccinated people with measles is hospitalised. Complications include pneumonia and brain swelling (encephalitis), and young children are most at risk.

facts.q: How well does the vaccine work?
facts.a: Two doses of MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles; one dose is about 93% effective. Children usually get doses at 12–15 months and 4–6 years.
A country has eliminated measles when no single chain of spread lasts 12 months or more. The US reached it in 2000. PAHO's regional commission decides whether a country keeps it.
